 1   Murphy, memorializing Governor Andrew M. Cuomo to 

 2   proclaim Tuesday, March 29, 2016, as Vietnam 

 3   Veterans' Day in the State of New York.  

 4                "WHEREAS, Members of the armed 

 5   services from the State of New York, who have so 

 6   honorably served this state and nation, deserve a 

 7   special salute from this Legislative Body; and 

 8                "WHEREAS, Every citizen of this 

 9   great state and nation is indebted to those brave 

10   individuals who served their country during the 

11   Vietnam War; and 

12                "WHEREAS, In recognition of the men 

13   and women who served with dignity and honor 

14   during this historic time period, let us remember 

15   them and thank them for their service; and 

16                "WHEREAS, Through more than a decade 

17   of combat, over air, land, and sea, these proud 

18   Americans upheld the highest traditions of 

19   United States Armed Forces; and 

20                "WHEREAS, The Vietnam War was fought 

21   in the Republic of South Vietnam from 1961 to 

22   1975, and involved North Vietnamese regular 

23   forces and Viet Cong guerrilla forces in armed 

24   conflict with the United States Armed Forces and 

25   the Army of the Republic of Vietnam; and 


                                                                1430

 1                "WHEREAS, The United States Armed 

 2   Forces became involved in Vietnam because the 

 3   United States government wanted to provide direct  

 4   military support to the government of Vietnam to 

 5   defend itself against the growing Communist 

 6   threat from North Vietnam; and 

 7                "WHEREAS, In 1961, members of the 

 8   United States Armed Forces began serving in an 

 9   advisory role to the government of the Republic 

10   of South Vietnam; as a result of the Gulf of 

11   Tonkin incidents on August 2, and August 4, 1964,  

12   Congress passed the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution 

13   (Public Law 88-408) on  August 7, 1964, which 

14   provided authority to the president of the United  

15   States to prosecute the war against North 

16   Vietnam; and 

17                "WHEREAS, In 1965, the United States 

18   Armed Forces ground combat units arrived in 

19   Vietnam; and 

20                "WHEREAS, More than 3 million 

21   servicemen and women left their families to 

22   bravely serve a world away in places such as 

23   la Drang to Khe Sanh, from Hue to Saigon, and 

24   countless villages in between; they pushed 

25   through jungles and rice paddies, heat and 


                                                                1431

 1   monsoons, fighting to protect the ideals we hold 

 2   dear as Americans; and 

 3                "WHEREAS, By the end of 1965, there 

 4   were 80,000 United States troops in Vietnam, and 

 5   by 1969, a peak of approximately 543,000 troops 

 6   were reached; an estimated 150,000 New York 

 7   soldiers served throughout the war; and 

 8                "WHEREAS, On January 27, 1973, the 

 9   Treaty of Paris was signed, requiring the release 

10   of all United States prisoners of war held in 

11   North Vietnam and the withdrawal of all 

12   United States Armed Forces from South Vietnam; 

13   two months later, the last 2,500 troops were 

14   withdrawn from South Vietnam, thus ending the 

15   United States' military involvement in the 

16   Vietnam War; and 

17                "WHEREAS, In 1984, New York was the 

18   first state in the nation to dedicate a Vietnam 

19   Veterans Memorial in Albany, New York, 

20   recognizing members of the United States Armed 

21   Forces who died or were declared missing in 

22   action in Vietnam; and 

23                "WHEREAS, Beginning on Memorial Day 

24   2012, the federal government began a partnership 

25   with local governments, private organizations and 


                                                                1432

 1   communities across the country to participate in 

 2   the commemoration of the 50th anniversary of the 

 3   Vietnam War, a 13-year program to honor and give 

 4   thanks to a generation of proud Americans who saw 

 5   our country through one of the most challenging 

 6   times; and 

 7                "WHEREAS, Chapter 90 of the Laws of 

 8   2008 designated March 29th of each year as 

 9   Vietnam Veterans' Day in the State of New York; 

10   the chapter designates that date as a day of 

11   commemoration to honor those individuals who 

12   sacrificed their lives for their country; and 

13                "WHEREAS, On May 25, 2012, President 

14   Barack Obama declared May 28, 2012, through  

15   November 11, 2025, as Commemoration of the 50th 

16   anniversary of the Vietnam War; and 

17                "WHEREAS, In addition, March 29, 

18   2016, has been chosen by the United States 

19   Department of Veterans Affairs to honor our 

20   nation's veterans; the observance of Vietnam 

21   Veterans' Day on this day is an appropriate way 

22   to honor those members of the United States Armed 

23   Forces who served in South Vietnam and throughout 

24   Southeast Asia during the  Vietnam  War; and 

25                "WHEREAS, The citizens of this great 


                                                                1433

 1   state and nation, benefactors of the sacrifices  

 2   and courageous acts of the men and women who 

 3   served and continue to serve in the United States 

 4   Armed Forces, remain indebted and are justly 

 5   proud of the Vietnam veterans from the State of 

 6   New York; now, therefore, be it

 8   Body pause in its deliberations to pay tribute to 

 9   the bravery, patriotism and sacrifice made by the 

10   men and women of the United States Armed Forces, 

11   both those still living and those who died in 

12   service to our great country; and to memorialize 

13   Governor Andrew M. Cuomo to proclaim Tuesday, 

14   March 29, 2016, as Vietnam Veterans' Day in the

17   Body pause further to encourage the people of the  

18   State of New York to observe Vietnam Veterans'

21   veterans deserve but did not receive upon

24                So when they got into the airplane 

25   and it rolled down the tarmac, they really were 


                                                                1435

 1   not sure where they were going and what they were 

 2   doing.  They got some new clothes, they got some 

 3   shots, they got some prescriptions to take, they 

 4   were given new uniforms and boots, they had some 

 5   good training, but they really didn't know what 

 6   lay ahead.  They went because their country asked 

 7   them to go.  

 8                In this chamber we get to have a 

 9   political opinion.  When you're a member of the 

10   United States armed forces, you don't have a 

11   political opinion, you go because your country 

12   tells you they need you.

13                And they went.  It's a difficult 

14   thing for some veterans to come home even in the 

15   best of times, when your country supports what 

16   you've done, when there are spontaneous outbursts 

17   in airports applauding your service, when 

18   communities have parades.  But it's an entirely 

19   different thing to come home and not be sure how 

20   your country feels about your service.  So that 

21   plane trip back is entirely different.

22                You've gone through the travails of 

23   combat, as these gentlemen did, and they didn't 

24   know how their country would feel.  They weren't 

25   really sure -- did I do my job?  Did I do 


                                                                1436

 1   everything I could have done?  There was that one 

 2   time -- and it's a very difficult thing to then 

 3   touch down and not be receiving the welcome that 

 4   the generation before them, certainly their 

 5   parents' generation, the World War II generation 

 6   on whom that military was built, on their 

 7   shoulders, they weren't getting the same 

 8   reception.

 9                Today is a small step in saying to 

10   the men and women who served in Vietnam:  Thank 

11   you, and welcome home.  A welcome home that they 

12   didn't get in the airports but that we're giving 

13   them now in the Senate chamber in our Capitol.

15   our Assembly sponsor, Assemblyman DenDekker, put 

16   this resolution in to honor the men and women who 

17   served in the Vietnam crisis.  They did it, of 

18   course, for their nation and for the Constitution 

19   of the United States.  But they did it for their 

20   brother to their right and to their left who they 

21   stood side by side with.

22                I'm so very proud of the men and 

23   women of that generation, of that military, that 

24   fought an incredibly different difficult war, 

25   that was something that current generations can't 


                                                                1437

 1   possibly fathom.  But in a recent delegation in

 3   to Vietnam, we noticed that Ho Chi Minh City -- 

 4   Saigon -- had a thriving economy, a capitalist 

 5   free market system that was burgeoning.  It was 

 6   truly amazing.

 8   delegation came home from that trip, it was

18   this great state who served, who left not knowing
